proposals.before: Jingzhen said: "De he who launched the cause with utmost sincerity; Liusheng killed him on his own authority—if not executed, there can be no government.
proposals.after: Jingzhen said: "Deji launched the cause with utmost sincerity; Liusheng killed him on his own authority—if not executed, there can be no government.
proposals.reason: Literal English corrupts 德其/德基 as "De he"; the referent is Xu Deji (徐德基), as the idiomatic already recognizes.

proposals.before: Fortuitously today Heaven guides our hearts; you and others lower your hearts—we shall greatly restore Liang's line, trusting in fortune from the former emperor; how dare I not muster warriors to follow you!"
proposals.after: Fortunately today Heaven guides our hearts; you and others humble your hearts—we shall greatly restore Liang's line, trusting in fortune from the former emperor; how dare I not muster warriors to follow you!"
proposals.reason: Opening 傑 is corrupt/unnatural in the Chinese; literal "Fortuitously" is awkward and the sentence should read as a continuous reply without the stray sense of 傑.

proposals.before: He brought in Cen Wende as Vice Director of the Secretariat to handle confidential affairs.
proposals.after: He brought in Cen Wenben as Vice Director of the Secretariat to handle confidential affairs.
proposals.reason: Chinese 岑文本 is Cen Wenben (文本), not Cen Wende; the given name was mistranscribed in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: He brought in Cen Wende as Vice Director of the Secretariat, in charge of secrets.
proposals.after: He brought in Cen Wenben as Vice Director of the Secretariat, in charge of secrets.
proposals.reason: Literal English should likewise use Cen Wenben for 岑文本.

proposals.before: Xian sent Wen Shihong to block Xiaogong. They fought at the mouth of the Qing River; Xiaogong won a crushing victory, seized a thousand warships, and took Yichang, Dangyang, Zhijiang, and Songzi. The false Jiangzhou general Gai Yan surrendered his city.
proposals.after: Xian sent Wen Shihong to block Xiaogong. They fought at the mouth of the Qing River; Xiaogong won a crushing victory, seized a thousand warships, and took Yichang, Dangyang, Zhijiang, and Songzi. The false Jiangzhou general Gai Yanju surrendered his city.
proposals.reason: Chinese gives the full name 蓋彥舉 (Gai Yanju); idiomatic shortens it to Gai Yan.

proposals.before: Biography of Fu Gongduo. Fu Gongduo was a native of Linji in Qizhou.
proposals.after: Fu Gongduo was a native of Linji in Qizhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 輔公祏，齊州臨濟人 has no 'Biography of' header; idiomatic invents an English biography label.

proposals.before: In martial force he was wanting, yet in rhetoric he was ample. Men who steal the names of benevolence and righteousness to mislead the age and stir custom are precisely those the sages condemn without mercy.
proposals.after: Observing Xian, in martial force he was wanting, yet in rhetoric he was ample. Men who steal the names of benevolence and righteousness to mislead the age and stir custom are precisely those the sages condemn without mercy.
proposals.reason: Chinese begins 觀銑 ('observing Xian'); idiomatic drops the named subject and opens with a pronoun only.

proposals.before: An imperial edict sent the Prince of Yue Li Xiaogong to Jiujiang, the Lingnan envoy Li Jing down from Xuancheng, the Huai prefect Huang Junhan out of Qiao, and the Qi prefect Li Shiji up the Huai and Si to crush him.
proposals.after: An imperial edict sent the Prince of Yue Commandery Xiaogong to Jiujiang, the Lingnan Grand Ambassador Li Jing down from Xuancheng, the Huaizhou Area Commander Huang Junhan out of Qiao, and the Qizhou Area Commander Li Shiji by the Huai and Si to crush him.
proposals.reason: 總管 is Area Commander / general-in-chief, not prefect; 越郡王 is Prince of Yue Commandery; 嶺南大使 is Grand Ambassador.

proposals.before: Biography of Shen Faxing. Shen Faxing was a native of Wukang in Huzhou.
proposals.after: Shen Faxing was a native of Wukang in Huzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 沈法興，湖州武康人 has no biography header; idiomatic invents 'Biography of'.

proposals.before: Biography of Li Zitong. Li Zitong was a man of Yizhou.
proposals.after: Li Zitong was a native of Cheng in Yizhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 沂州承人 names county Cheng in Yizhou; idiomatic invents Biography header and drops 承.

proposals.before: Li Zitong—Li Zitong was a man of Yizhou.
proposals.after: Li Zitong was a man of Cheng in Yizhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 沂州承人 includes Cheng (承); literal omits the county name.

proposals.before: Zuocai Xiang grew wary of him, and Zitong marched his forces south across the Huai to ally with Du Fuwei.
proposals.after: Caixiang grew wary of him, and Zitong marched his forces south across the Huai to ally with Du Fuwei.
proposals.reason: Chinese 才相 is the given name of Zuo Caixiang already introduced; idiomatic wrongly fuses surname+given as 'Zuocai Xiang'.

proposals.before: When he heard that Prince Yue Yang Tong had been set up at Luoyang, he sent a memorial styling himself grand marshal, recorder of the masters of writing, and Duke of Tianmen, and issued edicts appointing a full bureaucracy: Chen Guoren as minister of education, Sun Shihan as minister of works, Jiang Yuanchao as left vice-president of the masters of writing, Yin Qian as left assistant, Xu Lingyan as right assistant, Liu Ziyi as vice director of selections, and Li Baiyao as a secretarial officer.
proposals.after: When he heard that Prince of Yue Tong had been set up, he sent a memorial styling himself grand marshal, recorder of the masters of writing, and Duke of Tianmen, and issued edicts appointing a full bureaucracy: Chen Guoren as minister of education, Sun Shihan as minister of works, Jiang Yuanchao as left vice-president of the masters of writing, Yin Qian as left assistant, Xu Lingyan as right assistant, Liu Ziyi as vice director of selections, and Li Baiyao as a secretarial officer.
proposals.reason: Chinese 越王侗 is Prince of Yue Tong; idiomatic invents 'Yang' and 'at Luoyang' not in this unit.

proposals.before: Zhu Can was born in Chengyi, Bozhou.
proposals.after: Zhu Can was born in Chengfu, Bozhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 城父 is Chengfu, not Chengyi; the place name was mistranslated.

proposals.before: Zhu Can was a native of Chengyi in Bozhou.
proposals.after: Zhu Can was a native of Chengfu in Bozhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 城父 is Chengfu, not Chengyi; the place name was mistranslated.

proposals.before: After another victory over Shen Faxing he seized Jinling, installed Li Baiyao—once Faxing's clerk—as Vice Director of the Secretariat to draft state papers, and Yin Qian as Director of Ceremonies to oversee ritual music; learned men across the lower Yangtze flocked to his court.
proposals.after: After another victory over Shen Faxing he seized Jinling, installed Li Baiyao—once Faxing's clerk—as Vice Director of the Secretariat to draft state papers, and Yin Qian, formerly Left Assistant of the Imperial Secretariat, as Director of Ceremonies to oversee ritual music; learned men across the lower Yangtze flocked to his court.
proposals.reason: Chinese identifies 殷芊 as 尚書左丞 before appointment as 太常卿; the idiomatic English omits that prior office.

proposals.before: Yang Silin and Tian Zan of Xianzhou rose against him; neighboring districts joined in; defeated at Huaiyuan, Can fled with his survivors to Jutan and sued for peace.
proposals.after: Yang Shilin and Tian Zan of Xianzhou rose against him; neighboring districts joined in; defeated at Huaiyuan, Can fled with his survivors to Jutan and sued for peace.
proposals.reason: Chinese 士林 is Shilin, not Silin; the given name was mistransliterated.

proposals.before: Xianzhou leaders Yang Silin and Tian Zan raised troops against Can; neighboring commanderies responded; at Huaiyuan Can was greatly defeated, fled with his remnants to Jutan, and sent envoys to surrender.
proposals.after: Xianzhou leaders Yang Shilin and Tian Zan raised troops against Can; neighboring commanderies responded; at Huaiyuan Can was greatly defeated, fled with his remnants to Jutan, and sent envoys to surrender.
proposals.reason: Chinese 士林 is Shilin, not Silin; the given name was mistransliterated.

proposals.before: Shihong slipped to Bao'an Chengcheng Mountain, gathered deserters, and plotted a comeback; Yuanzhou men answered his call, but Zhang Shian uncovered the scheme and marched against him.
proposals.after: Shihong slipped to Bao'ancheng Mountain, gathered deserters, and plotted a comeback; Yuanzhou men answered his call, but Zhang Shian uncovered the scheme and marched against him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 保安城山 is Bao'ancheng Mountain (Bao'an-cheng shan); 'Chengcheng' wrongly doubles 城.

proposals.before: Shihong again fled to Bao'an Chengcheng Mountain, rallied stragglers, plotted renewed rebellion; Yuan men gathered in response; Zhang Shian detected it and marched troops to suppress him.
proposals.after: Shihong again fled to Bao'ancheng Mountain, rallied stragglers, plotted renewed rebellion; Yuan men gathered in response; Zhang Shian detected it and marched troops to suppress him.
proposals.reason: Chinese 保安城山 is Bao'ancheng Mountain; 'Chengcheng' wrongly doubles 城.

proposals.before: Qibi Khan gave him a wolf-head standard and named him Great Khan Dubi Qaghan, "Heaven-Solving Son of Heaven"; he led Turk forces into the Ordos and seized Yanchuan.
proposals.after: Shibi Qaghan gave him a wolf-head standard and named him Great Khan Dubi Qaghan, "Capable Son of Heaven"; he led Turk forces into the Ordos and seized Yanchuan.
proposals.reason: 始畢可汗 is Shibi Qaghan (not Qibi); 解事天子 means a capable/understanding Son of Heaven, not Heaven-Solving.

proposals.before: Qibi Khan sent him a wolf-head banner, titled him Great Khan Dubi Qaghan and "Understanding Heaven Son"; he then guided Turk troops to settle south of the Yellow River and took Yanchuan commandery.
proposals.after: Shibi Qaghan sent him a wolf-head banner, titled him Great Khan Dubi Qaghan and "Capable Son of Heaven"; he then guided Turk troops to settle south of the Yellow River and took Yanchuan commandery.
proposals.reason: Match 始畢可汗 as Shibi Qaghan and complete 解事天子 as Capable Son of Heaven.

proposals.before: While Song Jingang fought at Fenzhou with the issue still in doubt, he rejoined Liu Wuzhou.
proposals.after: While Song Jingang fought at Kuaizhou with the issue still in doubt, he rejoined Liu Wuzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 澮州 is Kuaizhou/Huizhou, not Fenzhou (汾州); the place name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: At the battle of Fenzhou with Song Jingang the outcome was still unsettled, so he again linked with Wuzhou.
proposals.after: At the battle of Kuaizhou with Song Jingang the outcome was still unsettled, so he again linked with Wuzhou.
proposals.reason: Match 澮州 as Kuaizhou rather than Fenzhou.
